title: Fraud and Fascism Attend Installation of US-aligned Colombian President
author: W. T. Whitney
content:
President Abelardo de la Espriella took office on August 7, in the process all
but completing Latin America’s turn to rightwing governments to political
power. Political arrangements in Colombia now are in sync with the US
government’s reassertion of power over the region with its National Security
[Strategy](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-
content/uploads/2025/12/2025-National-Security-Strategy.pdf) announced in
November, 2025.

In second-round presidential voting on June 21, 49.67% of the voters favored
De la Espriella, candidate for Colombia’s political rightwing. Iván Cepeda,
competing for the progressive Historic Pact Party, secured 48.7% of the vote.
The first round of voting for 13 candidates on May 31 had given 43.7% of the
vote to De la Espriella and 40.9% to Cepeda.

Cepeda is a senator, prominent human rights advocate, and son of a Communist
party leader murdered by paramilitaries. Outgoing President Gustavo Petro had
founded and led the Historic Pact Party. His government was the only
progressive government ever to serve in Colombia since independence from
Spain.

The Petro government’s record on advancing social programs was mixed. It
failed to achieve Petro’s prime goal of “total peace.” Despite the 2016 peace
agreement between Colombia’s government and the FARC leftist insurgents, armed
insurgencies and criminal gangs, heirs to the former paramilitary plague,
still ravage the countryside.

The current political background is of gigantic social and wealth
inequalities, militarization, continuing narco-production and trafficking, and
decades of massive killings and population displacements.

Rightwing forces had much at stake in the voting; For them, it was a watershed
moment. Their intensity of purpose showed in the extraordinary measures taken
to win the elections and keep another left-leaning government from taking
power

**Fraudulent election**

At a press conference on August 3, President Gustavo Petro charged that more
than 120,000 handwritten electoral documents sent to national electoral
officials from 1350 polling stations had been altered. Each polling station
creates and fills out one such form, the so-called E-14 form, as a record of
votes cast at each polling table. Petro indicated, in making this claim, that
he was relying on investigations carried out at the polling stations by
[70,000](https://mronline.org/2026/08/05/gustavo-petro-exposes-algorithmic-
manipulation-in-colombian-elections/) individuals with the assistance of 1000
computer experts.

The investigators allegedly discovered that individual votes had been changed
at the polling stations, supposedly by partisans of De la Espriella
officiating there. They found that out of 350,000 E-14 forms that were
examined and scanned, more than 122,000 of them had been “[systematically
reprocessed](https://mundoobrero.es/2026/08/04/gustavo-petro-denuncia-fraude-
electoral-y-declara-a-abelardo-de-la-espriella-presidente-ilegitimo/)
stripping them of their metadata and digital security seals—the hash locks.”
The E-14 forms then materialized under the label “page not scanned” and were
“published with different information and also with inconsistent signatures.”

According to Petro, the investigators discovered altered voter rolls showing
[municipalities](https://mundoobrero.es/2026/08/04/gustavo-petro-denuncia-
fraude-electoral-y-declara-a-abelardo-de-la-espriella-presidente-ilegitimo/)
claiming more voters than residents. These were located in Boyacá, Santander,
Antioquia, and Cundinamarca departments and also in the “coffee growing axis”.
These were precisely the regions that gave candidate De la Espriella his lead
of [751,000 votes](https://mundoobrero.es/2026/08/04/gustavo-petro-denuncia-
fraude-electoral-y-declara-a-abelardo-de-la-espriella-presidente-ilegitimo/).

A text from Petro said that, “For the first time, [electoral
fraud](https://mronline.org/2026/08/05/gustavo-petro-exposes-algorithmic-
manipulation-in-colombian-elections/) is achieved through the use of software
and algorithms. The world takes the message that [electoral] choice can be
manipulated through such software. According to
[TeleSur](https://mronline.org/2026/08/05/gustavo-petro-exposes-algorithmic-
manipulation-in-colombian-elections/), “Petro affirmed that the logistics and
financing of this fraud involved foreign resources and interests … [also] that
the National Electoral Council lacks the technical tools to identify these
anomalies in the software.”

The now former president suggested that the Israeli cyber-intelligence firm
BlackCore had [carried out](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/colombias-petro-
accuses-israeli-cyberfirm-blackcore-of-election-interference/3994677) the
electronic manipulation. He had earlier
[accused](https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/20260711-colombias-petro-accuses-
israeli-cyberfirm-blackcore-of-election-interference/) that firm of having
“deployed 500,000 bots—fake profiles—to manipulate the Colombian electorate.”
Colombian election officials defended the transparency and security of their
election processes. Electoral observers from the Organization of American
States and the European Union did likewise.

**A different kind of guy**

The rightwing political parties opposing presidential aspirant Cepeda had one
other extraordinary tool in their bag, specifically, their own presidential
candidate.

De la Espriella is a citizen of the US, Colombia, and Italy. He lived in Miami
for ten years, until 2026. There he gained great wealth, from two sources. As
a lawyer, he defended accused Colombian paramilitaries politicians accused of
corruption, and other criminals. As a wine and rum impresario, he prospered
greatly and then crashed in 2026; he owes almost [$1
million](https://www.financecolombia.com/after-losses-abelardo-de-la-
espriellas-rum-brand-pulls-out-of-united-states/). The new president owns
homes in Miami, Italy, and Colombia.

De la Espriella is a defender and friend, a childhood buddy, of the renowned
and death-dealing former paramilitary chieftain Salvatore Mancuso. He and his
family have personal and political ties with the brutal and lawless former
Colombian president Alvaro Uribe (2002-2012), himself accused of ties with
narcotraffickers and paramilitaries. As a younger man, the now 48-year-old de
la Espriella formed the Foundation for Peace Initiatives purposed for
extolling and recruiting paramilitaries. As president he promises to set up 10
mega prisons as per Bukele of El Salvador

De La Espriella expands anyone’s image of a potential president. His [business
website](https://delaespriellastyle.com/) proclaims that, “Defensor (Defender
Rum) is art in the form of rum, created by Abelardo De La Espriella and
Silvestre Dangond …This bottle of rum is a reminder that only those who dare
to challenge history are the ones who write it. Are you ready?”

And this: “Charming, irreverent, passionate, and a true connoisseur, Abelardo
De La Espriella—founder of Dominio (domain) De La Espriella and the law firm
De La Espriella Lawyers—is synonymous with success, integrity, and
determination … [T]his Renaissance man—with a Caribbean heart and a
Mediterranean spirit—is an entrepreneur, writer, singer, lawyer, and public
figure who has shattered all the conventions of fame to become a true role
model for millions of people.”

**Going the extra mile**

De La Espriella as president may well notch a feat extraordinary in itself.
The linkage between Colombia’s government and US imperialism is already
exceedingly tight. But the new president’s personal disposition and record
suggest he is well equipped for adding even more cement to US-Colombian
relations.

He has a lot to build on. The US government for decades provided financial and
material support for Colombia’s military operations against leftist insurgents
─ often under the pretense of fighting narcotraffickers. The US military had
recommended that the Colombian government rely on paramilitaries to control
the countryside. Thereafter, the US would be providing indirect support for
the paramilitaries, while turning a blind eye to their murdering and mayhem.
US Plan Colombia ((2000-2015) represented the high point of perennial US
financial support and material aid for Colombia’s military. The US military
has maintained up to eight air bases in Colombia, deployed troops and
contractors there, and trained Colombian troops. The US helped design and
finance Colombia’s prison system.

De La Espriella took the stage in 2023 when, living in Miami, he became a US
citizen. He donated to the Republican Party and was
[invited](https://justiceforcolombia.org/who-is-de-la-espriella-the-colombian-
far-rights-presidential-candidate/) to Mar-a-Lago.

As a candidate, he promised to end diplomatic relations with US-targeted Cuba
and Nicaragua, and restore relations with Israel. In early 2026, De la
Espriella [met privately](https://justiceforcolombia.org/who-is-de-la-
espriella-the-colombian-far-rights-presidential-candidate/) in Washington with
Secretary of State Rubio; he indicated ominously on social media that,
“important things are discussed in secret.” The State Department honored his
ascent to power on August 7 by, on that day, awarding Colombia $1 billion; it
goes toward “achievement of our shared objectives.”

He anticipates US (and Israeli) military forces joining Colombian counterparts
in fighting crime and narco-trafficking. Colombia will be part of the US
government-sponsored [Shield](https://www.chathamhouse.org/2026/03/trumps-
shield-americas-coalition-destined-fail) of the Americas, a collection of
rightwing Latin American and Caribbean governments cooperating with US plans
for regional dominance.

De La Espriella’s investiture as president took place in Cali, not in the
nation’s capital Bogota. He gave his inaugural address to soldiers assembled
at a nearby army base, not to civilians. He thereby gave notice of his
government’s “iron fist” and of Colombia as accomplice of aggressive US
imperialism.

Colombian Communist Party organization secretary Jorge Gómez,
[interviewed](https://nelsonlombanasilva.blogspot.com/2026/07/ante-el-
fascismo-de-la-espriella-ni.html#more) by Party member Nelson Lombana Silva,
summarizes:

> “[W]e …must understand that this is a new era … This has been the most
> important electoral result in all the history of the left.”
>
> “The inauguration is a new moment, one ushered in by fraud … but also
> fundamentally by something very special: the rise of a fascist far-right
> movement.”
>
> De la Espriella “will try to roll back social reforms—the gains the people
> have made in land ownership, health care, education, and the democratization
> of the state apparatus”
>
> De la Espriella must “inform the country of the scope of the oath he took to
> become a U.S. citizen … [and] to disclose whether he is a member of any U.S.
> intelligence agency.”
>
> “We’re going to have to make significant progress toward the idea of a Broad
> Anti-Fascist Front that confronts authoritarianism, anti-human- rights
> forces, and anti-reform forces … And a second major strategy… is the concept
> of so-called Civil Disobedience.”
